options.plan: Upstream release 26.8.0; upstream workforce entitlement and commercial support unverified
options.region: Operator-selected hosting and upstream tenant; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Realm-scoped generic OIDC broker, fixed Okta org issuer; first-login JIT; no SCIM pairing or SaaS bridge verified

conditions: Select a realm-scoped generic OIDC broker using Authorization Code, client authentication, an exact issuer and signature validation with the matching JWKS; this is a protocol-based proposal, not vendor-certified or runtime-tested interoperability.

Register an Okta Web app with the broker callback and intended user assignments per https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/create-an-app-integration/openidconnect/main/; choose the fixed org authorization server described at https://developer.okta.com/docs/concepts/auth-servers/, not an inherited custom/default issuer.

Only the Keycloak source is release-pinned; upstream documentation is mutable and dated. Upstream workforce entitlements, hosting costs and commercial support remain unverified; this is not a zero-cost guarantee or a change to AuthWeave authentication.

evidence.summary: The pinned broker guide documents generic OIDC code-flow configuration and issuer/signature checks. Selecting an Okta org as upstream is a conditional protocol-based proposal, not a verified pair.

conditions: Enable Create User If Unique in the selected first broker login flow; local user creation and identity linking occur at login, not through background provisioning, and can be disabled independently of realm self-registration.

Review profile requirements, identifier collisions and proof of control for existing accounts; do not enable unverified automatic email-based linking. Login-time JIT does not establish SCIM deactivation or consuming-app session revocation.

evidence.summary: The first-login flow can create a unique local user or require verification when linking an existing account. Its automatic-linking warning prevents interpreting JIT as safe unconditional account matching or lifecycle synchronization.

conditions: Native realm SCIM server support does not verify this Okta provisioning pair: endpoint authorization, upstream entitlement, identity correlation with the brokered user and operation compatibility still need pair-specific evidence and tests. UNKNOWN is not UNAVAILABLE.
Do not inherit native SCIM OPTIONAL, Auth0-specific mappings, SAML connector prerequisites or any Group Push claim into this generic OIDC scope; use a separate reviewed provisioning configuration.
Inbound provisioning into Keycloak is not outbound SaaS provisioning; deactivation, authorization and consuming-app session enforcement remain separate and untested.

evidence.summary: The release documents a realm-scoped SCIM server for external provisioners. It does not establish Okta entitlement, broker/SCIM identity correlation or a tested provisioning configuration for this selected login scope.

conditions: OIDC claim mappers import or update data at login according to sync mode; login claims and Okta application assignment do not establish background group lifecycle, Group Push or deprovisioning.

Native SCIM Group resources are a separate interface, not proof of this pair; group membership, deletion, nested-group behavior and downstream SaaS permissions require separate evidence. No external bridge is selected.

evidence.summary: Broker mappers describe first-login import and repeated-login updates. This does not establish group lifecycle synchronization from Okta or enforcement in a consuming application.
